cohort: The cohort consisted of 500 parturients at the Third Department of Obstetrics and Gynecology, School of Medicine, Faculty of Health Sciences, Aristotle University of Thessaloniki, Greece.
finding: The study characterized ultrasonographic labor patterns in a Greek population, revealing distinct changes in AoP and HPD throughout labor and demonstrating the utility of ultrasound in objectively assessing labor progression.
mod_finding: Cesarean section cases showed a slower increase in AoP and a slower decrease in HPD compared to vaginal deliveries, were associated with higher maternal BMI, and had longer total labor duration and higher birth weight.
